ET-M3-1.statement: Generation runs only from known sim scenes, with the initial state and asset hashes saved first; a scene-consistency check rejects injected mismatches.
ET-M3-1.candidate: a candidate is (i) a candidate manifest: the snapshot manifest's task id and version, seed, asset sha256s, cube half size and colour, and goal position; (ii) frames 0 to T of one recorded episode on that scene, rendered at 512 x 512 from the human render camera, frame 0 after restore_state and frame t after control step t; and (iii), for frame eligibility only, the joint positions and cube position that restore_state of the scene's saved initial state returns, the human render camera's centre (the translation of the snapshot manifest's cam2world_gl), and the candidate's actions a_1 to a_T, a_t being the pd_joint_pos target applied at control step t. An injection alters frames and the manifest, never (iii). No generator exists yet, so physics frames stand in for generated frames.
ET-M3-1.size_checkable_frames: The sightline is the segment from the camera's centre to the cube's initial centre. The arm's skeleton at a joint vector is vishwaroop.sim.so100_kinematics.arm_segments: segments from the base through each joint origin in chain order to the fixed jaw's frame, then to the fixed jaw tip, and through the moving jaw's origin to its tip, from the URDF chain. Its clearance is the shortest distance from any skeleton segment to the sightline. Frame 0 is size-checkable when the clearance at the initial joint positions is more than 0.035 m; frame t >= 1 when frame t - 1 is and the clearance at a_t (all six values) is more than 0.035 m. So the size-checkable frames are frames 0 to n - 1, n between 0 and T + 1: the frames before the arm first targets a pose near the sightline. Because the sightline ends at the cube's centre, a clearance above 0.035 m also keeps every skeleton segment more than 0.035 m from the cube's centre, so in those frames the arm has not been commanded onto the cube; the skeleton is lines without the links' thickness, so the pilot checks this premise in the simulator (stop 2). No image, mask or cube-area measurement enters this rule, so a resized, removed or duplicated cube cannot change which frames are size-checkable.
ET-M3-1.episode_kind: on even seeds the nominal scripted demo (VARIANTS['nominal']); on odd seeds an operator episode, m3-synth-lateral-miss and m3-synth-close-high alternating by seed, drawn as F2's rule in evals/M3-exit-tests.json
ET-M3-1.tolerance_pilot: block 10 seeds 10300 to 10319, used for nothing else, with the same nominal and operator alternation. The masks (red: R > 120, G < 60, B < 60; green: G > 120, R < 80, B < 80; 8-connectivity) and the rule are protocol-1's: each tolerance is the pilot's observed extreme widened by 10%, the band subject to 0.36 < a_lo and a_hi < 2.56. The band's extremes are taken over size-checkable frames only; the merge radius, first-frame tolerance, goal-centroid distance and minimum green count over every frame, as before. The pilot also records each candidate's n and the simulator's cube position after every step. It stops, writes nothing to evals/, and the owner is told before any control or injection is generated, if (1) any pilot candidate has no size-checkable frame t with 1 <= t <= T - 1; (2) in any size-checkable pilot frame the simulator's cube centre is more than 0.005 m from its initial position; (3) the widened band is not inside the limits; or (4) a snapshot render shows no cube or no goal. Otherwise the tolerances go to evals/M3-checker-tolerances.json with protocol_version m3-protocol-2 and sightline_clearance_m 0.035, and its sha256 is recorded in the status ledger before any control or injection is generated.
ET-M3-1.controls: 60 unmodified candidates on block 10 seeds 10400 to 10459
ET-M3-1.injections: 10 of each of six types, seed = 10200 + 10 x (t - 1) + i for type t = 1 to 6 and i = 0 to 9, each injected into its own unmodified source candidate on that seed, exactly as evals/M3-exit-tests.json's ET-M3-1 'injections' describes, with one change. rng = random.Random(seed); its first draw is the injection step: rng.randrange(1, T) for types 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, and for type 3 (cube resized) rng.choice of the list of size-checkable frames t with 1 <= t <= T - 1, in ascending order. If that list is empty the type-3 injection is not built and counts as not rejected. Every later draw follows in protocol-1's order. Type 6 replaces frame 0 by the snapshot render of seed + 500 (seeds 10750 to 10759), rendered for this purpose only.
ET-M3-1.checker: deterministic, with no learned part: the candidate manifest's fields equal the snapshot's; every frame has the render's shape; frame 0 equals the snapshot's saved render within the first-frame tolerance; in every size-checkable frame, the red components within the merge radius of the largest one's centroid together have an area within [a_lo, a_hi] x the snapshot render's cube area; in every frame, no other red component of at least 0.25 x that area exists; and in every frame with at least the pilot's minimum count of green pixels, the green goal pixels' centroid is within the goal-centroid distance of the snapshot's. A candidate with no size-checkable frame (n = 0) fails the cube-area check: the checker does not pass a candidate whose cube size it could not check.
ET-M3-1.threshold: 100% of the 60 injected candidates rejected, an injection counting as rejected only when its unmodified source candidate passes every check and the injected one fails at least one (an injection whose source fails, or that is not built, counts as not rejected); and at most 3 of the 60 controls (5%) falsely rejected
ET-M3-1.if_it_fails: recorded as failed. A further revision needs m3-protocol-3, the owner's decision, a new tolerance pilot on block 10 seeds no protocol has used, and fresh controls and injections on new seeds
ET-M3-1.reported: rejections by type and by the check that caught each; every source candidate's own result; false rejections with their cause; the false-rejection count with its Wilson 95% interval; how often the size check runs: for every candidate (pilot, controls, sources) its n and frame count, and for the pilot, the controls and the sources the number of candidates with n = 0, the number with no size-checkable frame 1 to T - 1, the minimum, median and maximum n, and the share of all frames size-checked; each type-3 injection's step and T; the pilot's largest cube displacement in a size-checkable frame; what happens at n = 0 (above); and a statement that controls are physics renders, so this does not estimate false rejection on generated frames (ET-M3-2 measures that)
